title: The five headline figure tiles on Overview (Net leverage, Gross leverage, Interest coverage, Revenue, Cash) have no trace control, so a headline number cannot be traced to its source.
expected: One labelled trace control per figure (content-matrix CM-009; design-rubric D-06; AGENTS.md: one trace control per paragraph, row or figure). The Modules page draws the same kind of tile with a trace control (MetricGrid).
actual: Overview falls back to HeadlineFigures when the Financial foundation handoff has no 'Financials and credit metrics' table with Metric and Unit columns (the synthetic proof run, and any retained run without that table). HeadlineFigures draws a <dl> of tiles with no control: 0 buttons or links inside the five tiles; the only trace buttons on the page belong to paragraphs and module rows. The main path (CP-1 has a 'Financials and credit metrics' table with Metric and Unit columns; checked by rewriting the snapshot in the browser) draws MetricGrid tiles that do carry a trace control, with different tiles (liquidity, leverage and the method's long labels), so the fallback is the only path without one.
suggested_change: Give each HeadlineFigures tile a TraceControl bound to the catalogue figure's source (the catalogue metric already carries a `source` id), or build the tiles from the CP-1 table lines so MetricGrid supplies the trace.

title: After the reader chooses another module in the Modules navigator (link by keyboard, or the Module select at 390 px), keyboard focus drops to <body>.
expected: Focus goes somewhere sensible after a keyboard action: it stays on the chosen entry or moves to the new module's heading (design-rubric D-35, D-38).
actual: Navigator is remounted with `key={entry.output.id}`, so the focused link or select is destroyed; document.activeElement is BODY after Enter on a navigator link (1440 px) and after changing the Module select (390 px). Tab restarts from the top of the page. Tab links (Overview, Changes) do keep focus.
suggested_change: Keep the Navigator mounted across module changes (drop the key; reset only the section state) or focus the new module heading after a hash change.

title: Switching module keeps the previous module's scroll offset, so the new module opens part-way down its page instead of at its Bottom line.
expected: A different module is a different page and opens at its top, Bottom line first (CM-001: first thing on the module page).
actual: With the shell's main region scrolled 1,500 px on Financial foundation, a click on 'Downside' in the navigator changes the hash and content but main.scrollTop stays 1,500; Downside's Bottom line is 1,147 px above the viewport. Tab links reset the scroll to 0; module links do not. Same at 390 px (1,464).
suggested_change: On a module change scroll the main region to the top of the module page (or to its heading), as the tab links already do.

title: Below 1001 px the Module select navigates on every ArrowDown, so a keyboard user cannot browse the options without changing page each time.
expected: Changing a setting does not change the context until the choice is committed (WCAG 3.2.2 On Input; design-rubric D-35).
actual: Focus on the Module select then ArrowDown: the hash goes from #modules/CP-1 to #modules/CP-1A at once, the page content changes and focus drops to BODY, so the next ArrowDown does nothing.
suggested_change: Navigate on commit (a Go button, or on blur or Enter) or use a listbox pattern; or make the options links.

title: 'On this page' lists 'Key findings' on modules that wrote no Key findings (Financial foundation and other data modules); the entry scrolls to a table section.
expected: Matrix CM-006: Source readiness, Financial foundation and Peer benchmark owe only the Bottom line, their tables follow as the main content; an outline entry named Key findings must lead to Key findings (D-16: headings carry information).
actual: Navigator takes the first coded table section as `firstFinding` and labels it 'Key findings'. On Financial foundation the entry opens 'Financials and credit metrics'; the page has no Key findings heading.
suggested_change: Label the entry with the section's own title (drawingTitle(heading)) unless its heading is 'Key findings'.

title: The trace drawer prints a module code ('CP-0') in a sentence the service wrote: 'the Basis file is not in the CP-0 inventory'.
expected: No module code as a label or name in the inspector and its Basis items; the module's plain name instead (design-rubric D-13 part 1; ruling 2026-11-11 Amendment 2026-11-12). The code replacement for module-written text does not cover text the application writes.
actual: Every Basis that names a file the inventory lacks shows 'annual.txt p.2 · not in inventory' and 'the Basis file is not in the CP-0 inventory' in the drawer (Overview Key findings; 17 module pages). The note is service text (credit_os_chips.py) passed through sourceCitationNote without the name replacement.
suggested_change: Write 'Source readiness inventory' in credit_os_chips.py (the library test at tests/test_library_page_browser.py:1885 already expects that wording), or pass chip.reason through plainModuleNames in buildTrace.

title: Report error states give the reader no cause and no next step: a failed or unknown run reads 'The published report could not be loaded.', a network failure prints the browser's own 'Failed to fetch', and neither offers retry, Run activity or the Library.
expected: Error states are designed: a plain sentence for what happened and a way forward (design-rubric D-31). A run that never published (failed run) should say so and link to its Run activity.
actual: A failed run (404), an unknown folder (404) and a server 500 all show the same one-line alert; a dropped connection shows the raw `TypeError` text 'Failed to fetch'; the only control in the main region is the breadcrumb 'Library'. The page title is the generic 'Credit report'. Null snapshot reads 'No report was published for this run.'.
suggested_change: Map 404 to 'This run has no published report' with a link to /run/<id>, map network failure to a fixed sentence with a Retry button, and keep the raw message out of the page.

screen: /report/<run>#overview, run whose handoffs have no reader passages (partial)
title: A run in the earlier format or with changed methods is not labelled 'Earlier format' or 'Earlier methods' on Overview or Changes; neither string exists in the connected app.
expected: Content-matrix CM-048 and ruling H7: a run with no reader passages shows only what H5 can select, 'labelled Earlier format'; the app labels it in the Report history. CM-060: a run whose earlier run used earlier methods, or whose CP-8 handoff was written under changed method text, shows 'Earlier methods'.
actual: With every module's Bottom line heading replaced by 'Reader summary' (an earlier-format handoff), Overview shows the headline tiles, 'No credit view is available in the published handoffs for this run.' and a 'Bottom line by module' list of summary sentences, with no format label. `grep -rn 'Earlier format' web/src` finds no non-test match, so Report history has none either (that part belongs to C1). The snapshot carries `run.methodChanges` (the field the legacy library reads, apps/issuer-library/credit_os/web/views.js:1017); no web/src file reads it, and with methodChanges=['CP-2'] neither tab shows 'Earlier methods'.
suggested_change: Add an 'Earlier format' badge to the run frame and the Report history row when no handoff of the run has a Bottom line passage (H7 test).

title: One unbroken 336-character token in the lead Bottom line runs past the navy band and makes the main region scroll sideways.
expected: Long text wraps in full; a qualification is never truncated (design-rubric D-32). FindingParagraph already uses wrap-anywhere.
actual: The lead is drawn as an h2 with no wrap-anywhere; the h2 is 1,158 px wide with 3,702 px of content, main.scrollWidth 3,808 against 1,372 client width; the text is cut at the band edge.
suggested_change: Add wrap-anywhere (and min-w-0) to the BottomLine lead and rest.

title: The heading outline does not follow the page structure: the whole Bottom line paragraph is the h2 (no 'Bottom line' heading text), module sections are h2 siblings of the module name h2, and Changes has no h2 of its own in its first-run state.
expected: One h1 per page and headings in order that describe the structure (design-rubric D-36): module name h2, its sections h3; a heading that names the Bottom line.
actual: Overview: H2 'Overview', H2 '<the bottom line sentence>', H2 'Key findings'. Modules/CP-2A: H2 'Downside', H2 '<bottom line sentence>', H3 chart titles under that sentence, H2 'Key findings', H2 'Limitations', H3 'Monitoring sensitivities' under Limitations. Changes (no earlier run): H1, H2 'No earlier run to compare.'.
suggested_change: Render the band label as the heading and the lead as a paragraph; use h3 for sections on module pages.

title: A change card shows a positive difference without a sign ('0.80x') while the Overview tile for the same measure shows '+0.80x vs FY2023'.
expected: Sibling screens agree (design-rubric D-26); signature of the year-on-year difference is this-year-minus-last-year with the sign (D-45; signal.ts changeText adds '+').
actual: Changes.tsx passes `withUnit(measure.difference, unit)` (publishedReport.ts:381) which never adds '+'; negative differences carry '-', positive ones carry nothing.
suggested_change: Use changeText for the card's difference.

title: When CP-8 delivered, the same handoff is drawn twice: on the Changes tab and again as a module 'Changes since the last run' in the Modules navigator, counted in the Modules tab badge.
expected: AGENTS.md: CP-8's handoff is shown in the library's Changes page; content-matrix CM-114 puts it on Changes (and Evidence).
actual: With a CP-8 output in the run the Modules tab reads 'Modules 15', the navigator lists 'Changes since the last run' and its page draws the same Bottom line, Key findings and Limitations ledger as the Changes tab.
suggested_change: none: the owner decides whether CP-8 stays listed as a module; if not, filter it out of buildReportView.modules.

title: The Chart/Table and Cards/Table switches are role=radiogroup buttons whose arrow keys move focus without selecting and whose radios are both Tab stops.
expected: ARIA radio pattern: arrow keys move and select, one Tab stop for the group (design-rubric D-35). Component is shared (X1).
actual: Focus on Chart, ArrowRight: focus moves to Table, aria-checked stays false until Space; both radios have tabIndex 0. 32 radiogroups on the 14 module pages plus the Changes presentation switch.
suggested_change: Use a RadioGroup/ToggleButtonGroup with selection following focus, or label the control as toggle buttons (aria-pressed) instead of radios.

title: Controls repeat identical accessible names with no context: 'Show sources for this passage' (several per module page) and six links named 'Evidence' on Overview.
expected: Every control has a distinguishable name (design-rubric D-37).
actual: Overview has 'Evidence' x6 (five Dates-to-watch rows and the tab) and 'Show sources for this passage' x2; CP-6 has 5 of the latter. A screen-reader user cannot tell the paragraphs apart.
suggested_change: Name the control after its section, e.g. 'Show sources for Key findings'; name each date link after its event.

screen: /report/<run>#overview, lead other than the committee decision (full)
title: The disclosure that holds the lead's second Bottom line paragraph is always labelled 'Decision rationale', also when the lead is Fundamental credit or Earnings update.
expected: Labels carry information (design-rubric D-16); CM-037/038 name three possible leads.
actual: With CP-6 not assessable, CP-2 leads and its second paragraph sits behind a closed 'Decision rationale' disclosure; the paragraph is hidden by default on Overview.
suggested_change: Label it by the lead ('Credit view, continued') or show the second paragraph; the wording and the default state are the owner's.

screen: /report/<run>#overview, lead Bottom line that cites a source (partial)
title: When the lead Bottom line holds a source reference, the navy band is lost: the heading 'Bottom line' is followed by the five figure tiles and then a link 'Read this passage in Evidence'.
expected: Bottom line first and as the band (D-01, D-22, CM-001); figures follow it.
actual: drawSection falls to the generic card for a passage with a reference; `afterBottomLine` (the figure tiles) is placed between the card heading and the paragraph, so the tiles read as the bottom line. Cards sit inside a card.
suggested_change: Draw `afterBottomLine` after the paragraph in the fallback card, and keep the band with a 'Read in Evidence' link as its text.

title: The three 'no comparison' sentences (not produced, not compared, no comparison recorded) and the unreadable-comparison sentence carry no link; only the first-run state offers 'Open the Overview'.
expected: CM-051: a fixed sentence states the case; the service's reason is drawn on Evidence. The reader should be able to reach that reason (D-31).
actual: A page holding only a heading and one sentence, no action to the Overview or the Evidence where the reason is drawn.
suggested_change: Add 'Open the Overview' and 'Review comparison evidence' links to those states.

title: On Overview the trace control of each 'Bottom line by module' row sits alone on a third line under the paragraph, unlike every other paragraph where it sits at the right of the text.
expected: Sibling screens agree (design-rubric D-26); 13 identical stacked rows (D-03).
actual: Each of the 13 rows is title+badge, one sentence, then a lone icon button; the page is 4,171 px tall.
suggested_change: Put the PublishedSource control beside the sentence (flex row), as FindingParagraph does.

title: The Modules navigator's <aside> has no accessible name, so the page has two unnamed complementary landmarks (axe landmark-unique); the 'Modules 14' tab has a name that does not contain its visible text 'Modules14'.
expected: Landmarks are distinguishable; accessible name contains the visible label (WCAG 2.5.3; design-rubric D-37).
actual: axe-core 4.x on 5 module pages at 1440 and 390 px: landmark-unique (moderate) and label-content-name-mismatch (serious, 'Modules 14', the frame's tab) on every page.
suggested_change: Give the aside aria-label='Module navigator'; give the count badge a leading space or build the label from the visible text.

title: A headline figure the module could not supply (Adjusted EBITDA FY2024, 'Not supplied') gets no tile and no stated gap; the reader cannot tell that it is missing.
expected: A missing value has its own form, never drawn as zero and never silently dropped (design-rubric D-14; CM-023); CM-044 allows only settled figures as tiles.
actual: HeadlineFigures drops any metric whose value is null (`figure?.value != null`); the proof handoff states 'Not supplied: the measure is not stated' for Adjusted EBITDA FY2024 and Overview shows five tiles and no note.
suggested_change: Show a gap tile ('Adjusted EBITDA: not supplied') or a one-line note listing the figures left out.

title: The change cards are cards inside the 'Changes since the last run' card.
expected: No cards inside cards; not every box is a card (design-rubric D-21).
actual: `section.card` (rounded border, shadow) wraps a grid of ChangeCard `li` boxes, each with its own border and radius; the same happens for the Cards/Table switch row. Overview figure tiles inside the fallback Bottom line card repeat it.
suggested_change: Let the cards stand on the page (heading outside any card) or use plain rows inside the section card.

title: Money is shown as 'US$m' on chart axes and 'USD millions' in tables but as '$2,250m' on tiles and change cards for the same figure; for GBP the tile reads '£1,250m' where the 2026-11-16 ruling names 'GBPm'.
expected: CM-320 and R-18: US$m for USD, otherwise the currency code and m (for example GBPm).
actual: withUnit maps USD to '$', GBP to '£', EUR to '€' (moneyUnits.cases.json is an owner-recorded answer key that expects those forms), while chart and table units read from the handoff.
probe: none: code read and the answer key; Overview tile '$2,250m' against the CP-1 chart axis 'US$m'
suggested_change: none: the owner chooses between the symbol form and the code form.

title: Dead and repeated work in the C3 files: `entryIndex` is threaded through ReportFindings, MetricGrid and ModuleConfidence into `traceForLine(_index)`, which ignores it; every row's Trace is rebuilt on each render; ChangeCard receives constants.
expected: Props that are passed are read; no work repeated per render without need (stage 6 sweep).
actual: traceForLine(snapshot, entry, _index, line) never reads _index; findingsTraces() builds a Trace per row on every render (no useMemo); Changes passes `direction: "none"` and `trace: null` for every card.
suggested_change: Remove the parameter and its three pass-throughs; memoise findingsTraces on (snapshot, entry, sections).

title: Overview draws no key charts and no 'Chart index' link, although the run holds data for catalogue rows that name Overview (Source readiness map, Credit-risk transmission, Monitoring triggers, issuer events).
expected: Ruling 2026-11-11 decision 3 and H5.4: key charts are repeated on Overview, those whose row in docs/visualisations/catalogue.csv names Overview in placement and for which the run has data; content-matrix CM-042; docs/design/2026-11-12-redesign-pass-1.md row 26 (Overview's 'Chart index' link opens Forecast).
actual: Overview shows headline tiles, the lead's Bottom line, Key findings, Contrary evidence, Bottom line by module, Limitations and Dates to watch; 0 charts, 0 figures, no chart index link. Fundamental credit (CP-2) owns 'Credit-risk transmission' and 'Monitoring triggers' on its module page, rows the catalogue places on Overview (CP-2-V02, CP-2-V03).
evidence: docs/visualisations/catalogue.csv (CP-0-V02, CP-1A-V01, CP-2-V02, CP-2-V03, CP-2D-V02, CP-5-V01, CP-MODEL-V02)
suggested_change: Select the catalogue's Overview rows for which the run has data and draw them under the lead (reusing the module-page components), with a 'Chart index' link to the Forecast tab; or record the drop in a ruling.

title: The Modules navigator has no search at its top.
expected: Ruling 2026-11-11 decision 5, content-matrix CM-028 and control-matrix CT-044: 'search sits at the top' of the navigator, beside the On this page outline and, on narrow screens, a labelled picker.
actual: The aside opens with the 'On this page' outline; 0 input, search or searchbox elements; the 14-module run is navigated by the list only. ModuleNav has no search code.
suggested_change: Add the search field to ModuleNav (filters the module list by plain name), or record that the owner dropped it.

title: When CP-8 delivered, Overview lists CP-8's Bottom line under 'Bottom line by module' and its limitations under 'Limitations', although CP-8's findings belong only on the Changes tab.
expected: Content-matrix CM-062: 'not shown (CP-8's findings are not on Overview)'; AGENTS.md: CP-8's handoff is shown in the library's Changes page.
actual: moduleBottomLines and runLimitations walk moduleOrder(run), which holds every module in run.modules including CP-8; the only skip is the lead. With a CP-8 output added to the run, Overview shows a 'Changes since the last run' row with 'Leverage fell, and the credit view improved.' and 'The earlier run did not state gross debt.' among the limitations. No test excludes CP-8 (reportView.test.ts has none).
suggested_change: Skip module 'CP-8' in moduleBottomLines and runLimitations (and in the Modules list if the owner drops the duplicate, C3-012).

title: The lead band on Overview is labelled 'Bottom line'; the ruling and the matrix name its kicker 'Credit view' ('Earnings view' on an Earnings Update).
expected: Content-matrix CM-037 ('lead section kicker Credit view') and CM-038; ruling 2026-11-11 H5 amendment 2026-11-16: the kicker reads 'Earnings view' in place of 'Credit view'.
actual: findingLabel() returns the section heading 'Bottom line' unless overviewLabel is set; only CP-1B sets it ('Earnings view'). 'Credit view' appears nowhere in web/src.
suggested_change: Pass overviewLabel='Credit view' for CP-6, CP-2 and CP-L10 leads (a wording choice the owner may confirm).

title: On a module page the charts, event lanes and maps come between the Bottom line and Key findings, pushing Key findings, Contrary evidence and Limitations 1,200 to 1,600 px down.
expected: Content-matrix CM-002 (Key findings after Bottom line) and CM-005: reading order Bottom line, Key findings, Contrary evidence and what would change the view, Limitations, then typed records, figures and tables; AGENTS.md voice standard: judgement first.
actual: ModuleFindings passes the confidence tile and the whole `#module-figures` block as `afterBottomLine`. Key findings starts at 2,279 px on Downside, 1,885 px on Rates, FX and hedging, 1,346 px on Liquidity and 1,620 px on Legal and covenants; the figures block is 1,603, 1,209, 670 and 944 px tall. The navigator also lists 'Figures and records' second, so the order is deliberate in code but not in the matrix.
suggested_change: Pass the figures block after the Limitations section (or the owner confirms charts-first and the matrix is amended). The decision changes what the reader sees first.

title: A chart's Table form omits the 'Basis and limitation' column, so a row's limitation (for example 'gross debt includes finance leases') is visible only inside the trace drawer, while the same column is drawn in plain tables on the same page.
expected: Content-matrix CM-025: every chart has a table form carrying the same published rows, unit, basis and source line; AGENTS.md: delivery keeps every number and qualification exact; design-rubric D-32 (a qualification is never truncated).
actual: Leverage Table form shows Period, Total debt / EBITDA, Net debt / EBITDA and a Source control; the handoff row's 'Basis and limitation' ('Synthetic.') appears only in the drawer ('Basis and limitation — Synthetic.'). `chartTable` filters the column out when evidence is in the drawer, whereas 'Net debt data' on the same page prints 'Synthetic; gross debt includes finance leases.'. The code is in visuals/ (C4) and shows on C3 module pages.
suggested_change: Keep the limitation text of the column in the Table form (a note under the chart), leaving only the source reference to the drawer.

title: The document title is 'Modules — <issuer> — Credit OS' for every module, and a module change is neither focused nor announced.
expected: A page title that identifies the content (WCAG 2.4.2) and a status change announced without moving focus (design-rubric D-43).
actual: Titles for Financial foundation, Downside and Committee decision are identical; after choosing a module there is no [aria-live], role=status or role=alert region on the page.
suggested_change: Add the module name to the title and move focus to the module heading (also fixes C3-002).

title: 'Compare with the 5% move' on Rates, FX and hedging is a <select> with one option ('10%'), so the control offers no choice.
expected: A control the reader can operate changes something; a one-choice selector is a fixed label (design-rubric D-03, D-35). The code is in visuals/MacroSensitivity (C4) and shows on this C3 module page.
actual: The select holds the single option '10%'; selecting it changes nothing (checked: content identical). The two Downside selectors ('Compare with', 'Cash-interest basis') have two options each and change the panel.
suggested_change: Draw the selector only when it has two or more options; otherwise print 'Compared with the 5% move: 10%'.

title: Text is set at 12 px on report pages: the Source readiness 'key limitation' reasons, the navigator's group captions, chart labels (70 SVG text nodes on Financial foundation) and the Committee decision limit labels.
expected: Nothing set below 13 px (design-rubric D-30); a qualification is never smaller or fainter than the text it qualifies (D-32).
actual: `text-xs text-text-tertiary` on the reason under each readiness group ('Only the synthetic filing is available', 'Financing terms are absent') is 12 px; 'On this page' and 'Modules in this run' captions are 12 px; every chart axis and value label is 12 px. The tab count badge is 12 px (a source component, exempt).
suggested_change: Raise those classes to the 13 px caption size; chart text is C4's.
